about: GATE-stamps' fixture table (ARCHITECTURE.md section 8.5): raw outputs drawn from executed runs, each with the stamp spine section 8.8 derives from it. An executed fixture names its run and quotes its lines verbatim; the gate fails unless every quoted line is a whole line of that run's record (verdict_lines, a configuration's verdict_lines, or an output file on disk), and one configuration of that run prints them all (a fixture names it in config when configurations of several checkers print the same lines), and every number in its context stands as a whole token in those lines or that configuration's verdict lines, command line, budget, values or exit code (a solver's rlimit is the one its budget records). A fixture marked "executed": false stands for a row of section 8.8 that no run on disk exercises yet, or whose run prints output no parser in this package reads yet (PostgreSQL's, until S6 and S7); its note names the run, and the gate reports those rows. An executed fixture is always read by one of the package's parsers (solver, tlc, lean, trace), never typed as a raw output. Engine and version always come from the configuration that printed the lines (its own, or the record's), never from the fixture.
